name: No Sound
description: Restore Windows audio by checking output, volume, connections, and built-in diagnostics.

identify_scope.question: Where is sound missing?
identify_scope.help_text: Testing more than one application helps determine whether the issue belongs to one app or to Windows audio.

test_system_sound.title: Test Sound in Another Application
test_system_sound.instruction: Play a familiar system sound or a trusted local media file in a second application. Keep the volume at a moderate level.

check_app_volume.title: Check the Application's Audio Controls
check_app_volume.instruction: Confirm the application or browser tab is not muted. Right-click the speaker icon, open Volume mixer, and confirm that the application volume is above zero.
check_app_volume.help_text: Windows can store a separate volume and mute setting for each application.

app_result.question: Can you hear the application now?

resolved_app.title: Application Audio Restored
resolved_app.message: The application's mute or volume setting caused the issue. Windows audio is working normally.

check_mute.title: Check Volume and Mute
check_mute.instruction: Select the speaker icon near the clock. Make sure audio is not muted and slowly raise the volume to a comfortable level. Also check any physical mute key or headset control.
check_mute.help_text: Software and hardware mute controls can operate independently.

resolved_controls.title: Sound Restored
resolved_controls.message: A volume or mute control was preventing playback. Audio is now working.

select_output.title: Select the Intended Audio Output
select_output.instruction: Select the speaker icon, open the output-device list, and choose the speakers or headset you intend to use. Disconnect an unused Bluetooth audio device if Windows keeps selecting it.
select_output.help_text: Windows may send sound to a monitor, dock, headset, or Bluetooth device that is not currently being used.

output_result.question: Does the selected device play sound?

resolved_output.title: Correct Audio Output Selected
resolved_output.message: Windows had been sending audio to another device. The intended speakers or headset are now active.

check_connection.title: Check the Speaker or Headset Connection
check_connection.instruction: Reconnect the headset, speaker cable, USB device, or dock firmly. If the device has power, turn it off and back on. Do not force a plug into an unfamiliar port.

connection_result.question: Is sound working after reconnecting the device?

resolved_connection.title: Audio Connection Restored
resolved_connection.message: Reseating or restarting the audio device restored its connection.

run_troubleshooter.title: Run the Windows Audio Troubleshooter
run_troubleshooter.instruction: Open Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters, then run Audio. Follow the recommended checks and restart only if prompted after saving your work.
run_troubleshooter.help_text: The built-in troubleshooter checks services and device configuration without requiring third-party software.

troubleshooter_result.question: Did the Windows troubleshooter restore sound?

resolved_troubleshooter.title: Windows Audio Repaired
resolved_troubleshooter.message: The built-in diagnostic corrected the audio configuration. Note its reported fix if the issue returns.

escalate.title: Audio Device Support Is Recommended
escalate.message: Record the selected output, connection type, device model, and troubleshooter result. A technician can safely examine drivers, services, hardware, or organizational settings.
